content:
Vectors reward the student who pictures them, not just pushes symbols. A dot product measures overlap. A cross product measures spread. So picture the vectors first, then compute. Try the free JEE Vector Algebra online test below. It carries 15 solved MCQs with instant scoring. Shoot for 12.

What JEE asks from vector algebra

  • Dot product for angle, and for perpendicular checks.
  • Cross product for area, and for direction.
  • Section formula for a dividing point.
  • Centroid from three position vectors.
  • Scalar triple product for volume and coplanarity.
  • Projection of one vector along another, and its sign.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Take a·b = |a||b| cos θ for the angle between vectors.
  • Use |a×b| = |a||b| sin θ for the area of a parallelogram.
  • Note a·b = 0 means the two vectors sit perpendicular.
  • Recall |a×b|² + (a·b)² = |a|²|b|² always holds.
  • Find a midpoint or centroid by averaging position vectors.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Confusing the dot product with the cross product.
  • Reading collinear as always the same direction.
  • Dropping the half in the triangle area formula.
  • Forgetting the cross product flips under a swap.
  • Squaring a magnitude, but dropping the dot term.

quiz.title: JEE Vector Algebra Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If two vectors are collinear, which statement is always false?
options: They are scalar multiples of each other
They must point the same way
questions.explanation: Collinear vectors run parallel, yet they may point opposite ways. So they need not point the same way.

questions.q: If a and b are unit vectors with angle θ, then |a − b| equals:
questions.explanation: |a−b|² = 2 − 2cos θ = 4 sin²(θ/2). Taking the root gives 2 sin(θ/2).

questions.q: For r = i + 2j + 3k, the direction ratios are:
questions.explanation: The scalar components of a vector are its direction ratios. So they are 1, 2, 3.

questions.q: The area of a parallelogram with diagonals 3i + j − 2k and i − 3j + 4k is:
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)|d₁ × d₂|. The cross product has magnitude 10√3, so the area is 5√3.

questions.q: P and Q have position vectors 3a − 2b and a + b. R divides PQ in 2:1 internally. R is:
For unit vectors a and b with angle θ, the maximum of |a + b| + |a − b| is:
questions.explanation: The sum equals 2cos(θ/2) + 2sin(θ/2). Its maximum is √(4+4) = 2√2.

questions.q: Vertices have position vectors i + j, j + k and k + i. The centroid is:
questions.explanation: The centroid is the average of the three vectors. That gives (2i + 2j + 2k)/3.

questions.q: Vector a has dot products −1, 6, 5 with 3i − 5k, 2i + 7j and i + j + k. Then a is:
questions.explanation: Set a = xi + yj + zk and solve the three equations. This gives x = 3, y = 0, z = 2, so a = 3i + 2k.

questions.q: The angle between i − 2j + 3k and 3i − 2j + k is:
questions.explanation: The dot product is 10 and each magnitude is √14. So cos θ = 10/14 = 5/7, and the first two options match.

questions.q: The locus of P with r·a = 0, for a fixed non-zero a, is:
questions.explanation: Every r with r·a = 0 stays perpendicular to a. Those points form a plane through the origin.

questions.q: If |a + b| = |a − b|, then a and b are:
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 4a·b = 0. So a·b = 0, which means a and b sit perpendicular.

questions.q: The angle between i + j and i is:
questions.explanation: cos θ = 1/√2 here. So the angle is 45°.

questions.q: The angle between i + j and i − j is:
questions.explanation: Their dot product is zero. So the angle is 90°.

questions.q: If |a| = 2, |b| = 3 and a·b = 4, then |a × b| equals:
A vector of magnitude 5 parallel to the resultant of 2i + 3j − k and i − 2j + k is:
questions.explanation: The resultant is 3i + j with magnitude √10. Scaling the unit vector by 5 gives (15i + 5j)/√10.
